findings.quote: that the seas are connected by channels because Chian and Thasian pottery is found in the Naro
findings.problem: Greek has a gap (***) after τὸ συντετρῆσθαι τὰ πελάγη; ἀπὸ τοῦ εὑρίσκεσθαι ('from the finding of') follows the gap, so the English supplies a smooth causal link the text does not preserve.
findings.proposed_fix: that the seas are connected by channels [gap in the Greek text] ... from the finding of Chian and Thasian pottery in the Naro

findings.quote: Artemidorus corrects this, and not unreasonably. According to him,
findings.problem: Greek has a gap marked after οὐκ ἀτόπως... ; the next sentence begins κατ᾽ ἐκεῖνον δὴ and English reads on as if the text were continuous.
findings.proposed_fix: Artemidorus corrects this, and not unreasonably ... [gap in the Greek text]. According to that authority (κατ᾽ ἐκεῖνον),

units.note: Numbers checked and correct: 535 miles, 4280 stades, 178, 267, 630, 3100, 7320, 180, 4000, 6500. Possibly corrupt, no fix given: 'τῶν νήσων τῶν Λιβυρνίδων Τιθείς' (the English 'among the Liburnian islands is Titheis' resolves a doubtful word, the name or participle, silently) and 'σταδίων καὶ πεντακοσίων' (the 'καὶ' suggests a lost numeral). The sentence 'Since the distance from Perinthus...' renders an excerpt-opening ὅτι as a causal 'Since'. The Greek simply lists the figures, and the units (stades) are not stated. This is not a finding, only a caution.

findings.quote: the poet’s words were literally true:
findings.problem: Greek: λοιπὸν ἦν τῷ ὄντι τὸ τοῦ ποιητοῦ 'Αἴγυπτόνδ᾽ ἰέναι…' means 'what remained, in truth, was the poet's line (to go to Egypt…)'. λοιπὸν ἦν is 'there remained', not 'were true', and τῷ ὄντι is 'in truth/indeed', not 'literally'. The English turns a statement of what was left into a claim that the verse was literally true.
findings.proposed_fix: all that remained, in truth, was the poet’s line:

units.note: Euergetes Physcon (Ptolemy VIII) is the right identity. Other points checked and sound.
